leif_verbatim: create comparisions between the real apple airtag and ours and show me eveyrthing. we must do a detailed pcb comparison and component comparison. first step is recreating it exactly.

target.note: Every Apple-side fact on this page is transcribed from that dossier with its own confidence tag carried through. Where the dossier says a thing is inferred or unverified, this page says so too. Nothing was re-researched by this lane; two things were re-READ off the photographs, and where that reading differs from the dossier it is marked.

verdict_vocabulary: the same part, or the same scheme built the same way. No design difference.
a different part doing the same job to the same specification. Chosen for sourcing, not for design reasons.
a deliberate design difference with a numbered decision behind it. Includes parts halo DELETED because their function moved somewhere else.
the function is absent from halo and nothing in halo replaces it.
halo has it and the AirTag does not. Counted separately; it is not a divergence from Apple, it is a departure from Apple.

components.function: MCU + BLE radio + NFC tag — the brain

apple.part: Nordic nRF52832-CIAA (nRF52832CIAAE)
apple.source: research/01 §3 U1 — Catley, iFixit, TechInsights; marking read off oflynn-backside-fullres.jpeg

components.why: The nRF54L10 brings Bluetooth Channel Sounding, which ranges tag-to-tag at 6-10 cm without a second radio, and it costs 61 cents LESS than the nRF52832 it replaces.

exact.buyable: Yes. nRF52832-CIAA is a live catalogue part; D12 priced it at $2.81 at a hundred.
exact.stack: WLCSP-50 is 3.0 x 3.2 mm against the QFN-48's 5.0 x 5.0 mm, so it FREES board area — but a WLCSP at 0.35 mm pitch needs finer design rules than this 0.127 mm / 0.09 mm board is quoted at, and the escape would have to be re-solved.
exact.cost: +$0.61 per unit at a hundred (D12's own figures: $2.81 for the nRF52832 against $2.20/$2.59 for the nRF54L05/L10).
exact.schedule: A full re-layout of the SoC block and a firmware port back to nRF52 — which is the direction every existing Find My implementation already runs, so the firmware half gets EASIER, not harder.
exact.loses: Channel Sounding, and with it peer-to-peer ranging between Leif's own devices — the one capability D1 says no consumer tag offers at all.

apple.part: Apple U1 (die TMKA75, TSMC 16 nm) in a USI SiP module
apple.marking: none legible; Apple's own FCC internal photo 6 labels this position "UWB Module"
apple.source: research/01 §3 U2 — Catley (die marking via siliconpr0n), iFixit, TechInsights

halo.text: NOT FITTED. J2 reserves eight SMD lands just inboard of the board edge (VDD, GND, SPI SCK/MOSI/MISO) as a stuffing option — a stub, not a DW3110 land pattern, because no sourced DW3110 pin table exists in this repo.

components.why: There is no ultra-wideband transceiver you can buy a hundred of: DW3110 shows 30 in stock, DW3220 shows 9, and the DW1000/DW3210/DW3120/DWM3000 all show zero — so the ranging function moved into the SoC's own radio instead.

exact.buyable: NO, AT ANY PRICE. The U1 is Apple-custom silicon in a USI system-in-package and is not sold to anyone. There is no drop-in and no grey channel for it. This is the single hard wall in the whole project.
exact.stack: n/a
exact.cost: n/a — not a money question.
exact.schedule: n/a.
exact.loses: Nothing halo has. The nearest CATEGORY substitute is a Qorvo/NXP DW3xxx, which D12 priced at +$8.86 per tag and which is neither pin-, protocol- nor Find-My-compatible; its driver licence also carries a Qorvo-silicon-only field-of-use clause that cannot sit inside AGPL firmware.

apple.part: Apple U1 + ANT3 + the 'Rose' coprocessor firmware, commanded over the 'Durian' L2CAP path
apple.source: research/01 §4 and §8 — SEEMOO's opcode list; the U1 holds its own 64-bit processor and side-loads its firmware from the shared flash

halo.text: ABSENT. Nothing in halo does this and nothing can.

components.why: Precision Finding needs Apple's silicon AND Apple's blessing — the MFi programme's terms make the specification Apple Confidential, so reading it and publishing an implementation cannot both happen.

exact.buyable: NO. Two independent walls: the U1 is not sold, and the certified path additionally needs a per-unit Apple Token burned at an MFi factory.
exact.stack: n/a
exact.cost: n/a.
exact.schedule: n/a.

apple.part: GigaDevice GD25LE32D (iFixit) or GD25LQ32C/GD25LQ32DLIGR (O'Flynn) — 32 Mbit (4 MB) SPI NOR, 1.8 V
apple.marking: none read; O'Flynn identified it from the 10-pad WLCSP pinout, J-Flash detected GD25LQ32C
apple.conf: primary, but the two teardowns name DIFFERENT part numbers
apple.source: research/01 §3 U3 — iFixit and O'Flynn disagree on the exact suffix

halo.text: DELETED. No external memory of any kind. Firmware lives in the nRF54L10's own 1.022 MB flash — measured at 13,164 bytes used, 1.27 percent.

components.why: Apple needed 4 MB off-die because the U1's own 'Rose' firmware is staged there too; with no U1 and 1.27 percent of the SoC's internal flash used, an external NOR would be a part, a bus and a power gate carrying nothing.

exact.buyable: The FAMILY is catalogue and costs cents. The exact part is NOT settled: iFixit says GD25LE32D, O'Flynn says GD25LQ32C, and those are different order codes. An exact recreation cannot choose between them from the public record.
exact.stack: A WLCSP-10 is small, but every square millimetre of the top face inside Ø21.2 mm has only 0.400 mm of clearance under the piezo diaphragm, and the bottom face is over the cell. Four SPI nets plus a gated 1.8 V rail would have to be routed on a board already carrying 255 track segments and 49 vias.
exact.cost: Cents for the part; this lane did not fetch a price and does not invent one.
exact.schedule: A schematic block, a re-layout of the SoC's south side, and a firmware driver for a memory holding 1.27 percent of what already fits on-die.
exact.loses: Nothing. It would be dead weight.

apple.part: Bosch Sensortec BMA280 (iFixit writes "BMA28x")
apple.marking: none legible in any photograph in images/airtag
apple.source: research/01 §3 U4 — Catley, iFixit, EDN

components.why: Same job, chosen on one number: 50 nA in its lowest-power mode, which is what a coin cell budget turns on.

exact.buyable: The part number is public and Bosch still lists the BMA280; NO STOCK OR PRICE WAS FETCHED by this lane, so its availability today is CANNOT DETERMINE.
exact.stack: The BMA280's 2.0 x 2.0 mm LGA and the LIS2DW12's 2.0 x 2.0 mm LGA-12 are the same body size, so the stack does not care. The PINOUT is not the same and the land pattern would be redrawn.
exact.cost: Unknown — not fetched. halo's LIS2DW12TR is $0.74 at a thousand.
exact.schedule: One footprint, one driver.
exact.loses: The BMA280's sleep current is not on file here, so whether the swap costs or saves current is CANNOT DETERMINE.

apple.part: Maxim MAX98357A class-D digital audio amp (iFixit writes MAX98357B)
apple.marking: none legible in any photograph in images/airtag
apple.source: research/01 §3 U5 — Catley and iFixit, who name different suffixes

halo.text: DELETED. Two SoC GPIO driven anti-phase into the bender, through R9 (100 R series damping).

components.why: A bridge-tied class-D swings about 6 Vpp from a 3 V cell and two GPIO driven anti-phase swing the SAME 6 Vpp; what the amplifier bought was CURRENT, and a piezo bender is capacitive — 1.43 mA peak at 21 nF and 3.6 kHz, inside nRF54L high-drive.

exact.buyable: The family is catalogue. WHICH PART is not settled — Catley says MAX98357A, iFixit says MAX98357B.
exact.stack: A WLCSP plus its bypass on a top face with 0.400 mm of clearance, or a bottom face already carrying the SoC, both crystals, the accelerometer, the inductor and four bulk capacitors.
exact.cost: Not fetched; not invented.
exact.schedule: A schematic block, an I²S link the firmware does not have, and a re-layout.
exact.loses: Nothing, and it would make the sounder WORSE: the amplifier was the right part for Apple's 8 Ω voice coil and is the wrong part for a capacitive bender. Restoring it only makes sense together with row 13, the voice coil.

apple.marking: none legible in any photograph in images/airtag
apple.source: research/01 §3 U7 — Catley, iFixit

components.function: Bulk energy storage — hold-up through the battery-removal reset, and speaker transients

apple.part: 5 x 100 uF electrolytic/tantalum. NO PART NUMBER PUBLISHED.
apple.package: large SMD bricks around the front rim
apple.marking: J107S — read off oflynn-frontside-fullres.jpeg by this lane; all five located and counted
apple.conf: primary for the count and the marking, none for the part
apple.source: research/01 §3 C1–C5 — Catley, EDN

halo.note: 4 x 10 uF 0402 = 40 uF, against Apple's 500 uF. One twelfth of the bulk.

components.why: A 100 uF part is a brick and the top face inside Ø21.2 mm allows a 0.400 mm body, so Apple's rim capacitors do not physically fit under halo's diaphragm gap; halo's four sit on the BOTTOM face over the cell where 0.578 mm is allowed and they clear by 0.028 mm.

exact.buyable: The VALUE is buyable; the PART is not identified — "J107S" is a marking, not an order code, and no teardown names the manufacturer.
exact.stack: THIS IS THE BLOCKING ONE. No 100 uF capacitor exists at the 0.33 mm body height that D22 measured as the ceiling on the top face, and Apple mounts its five on the FRONT rim of an annular board that halo does not have. Fitting them means the annular outline (row PCB-4) and the carrier come back too.
exact.cost: CANNOT DETERMINE for the part. The stack cost is the whole of D17's 1.742 mm recovery.
exact.schedule: A full mechanical re-budget, not a BOM change.
exact.loses: Whether 40 uF holds halo up long enough for a five-removals reset is NOT MEASURED here — the VBAT_SNS net and TP7 exist for exactly that test and the test has not been run. CANNOT DETERMINE.

apple.part: 0201/0402 R, L, C including the antenna matching networks, plus K11-marked Schottky diode pairs mid-ring. NO VALUES PUBLISHED.
apple.marking: K11 on the diode pairs; the passives carry none
apple.conf: primary for their existence, none for their values
apple.source: research/01 §3 — O'Flynn/Catley photographs

halo.text: SAME PACKAGE CLASSES, for the same reason Apple used them. The counts below are read off the resolved bill of materials, not asserted: 0201 dominates and the only 0402s are the four bulk capacitors on the bottom face, which is the one place the height allowance reaches 0.578 mm. The 2.4 GHz matching network is NORDIC'S reference values, not a copy of Apple's — Apple's values are published nowhere.

components.why: Same package classes for the same reason — height, not money: an 0201 body is 0.33 mm and fits the 0.400 mm allowance, an 0402 body is 0.55 mm and misses by 0.15 mm.

exact.buyable: The parts are catalogue; APPLE'S VALUES ARE NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE. No teardown reads a matching network off the board. An exact recreation would have to measure every passive on a physical AirTag.
exact.stack: Already matched.
exact.cost: $0 — halo is already in the same package classes.
exact.schedule: Would need a physical part, an LCR meter and a lot of desoldering.

apple.part: Inverted-F, LASER-DIRECT-STRUCTURED onto the plastic antenna carrier and soldered to pads at the board edge. Max gain -3.2 dBi.
apple.package: LDS trace on a moulded interconnect device
apple.marking: Apple's own FCC internal photo 6 labels the position "Bluetooth Antenna"
apple.side: on the carrier, not on the board
apple.source: research/01 §3 ANT1 — Catley and Apple's FCC BLE test report E1V2

halo.text: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-05. halo's antenna number is CANNOT DETERMINE. The +0.521 dBi figure was a model of a PARAMETRIC PLACEHOLDER on a Ø30 mm study outline that is not this board — board.py says so itself under its own heading 'what this board does not claim'. And the comparison was never valid on its own terms: Apple's -3.2 dBi is a MEASURED figure for a SHIPPED antenna in an FCC test report. Differencing a measurement against a model of a placeholder produces a headline, not a result. ce-rf is solving THIS copper now.

components.why: Etched copper is free, travels inside the KiCad design block, and cannot tear off — Apple's carrier antennas are attached by six solder joints that break when the board is lifted.

exact.buyable: The GEOMETRY is not published — no teardown traces the LDS pattern. And LDS is a PROCESS, not a part: it needs a moulded thermoplastic carrier doped with an LDS additive, a laser-structuring pass and an electroless plating line.
exact.stack: It brings the plastic carrier back, and with it the soldered board-to-carrier joints, and D17's flat-inside shell would have to become Apple's carrier-plus-shell pair.
exact.cost: CANNOT DETERMINE — no LDS quote was retrieved by this lane or by any other in this repo. For scale, D13 prices a single-cavity aluminium tool for ONE plain moulding at $1,500-3,000 and two-shot tooling at $45,000-95,000; an LDS carrier needs its own tool plus the structuring and plating steps on top.
exact.schedule: Tooling lead time plus a process qualification, against etched copper which ships on the same panel as the board.
exact.loses: 3.7 dB of modelled gain, by Apple's own published number against ce-rf's.

apple.part: LDS coil on the carrier with a return trace on the far side of the plastic and a via at each end. In the front photograph the central coil images as WOUND COPPER WIRE, not as a printed trace — this lane records that reading and does not resolve it against the dossier.
apple.package: coil on the carrier, around the magnet well
apple.marking: Apple's FCC internal photo 5 labels the position "NFC Antenna"
apple.conf: primary for its existence and position; the winding technique is a CONFLICT between the dossier's LDS description and what this lane sees in the photograph
apple.source: research/01 §3 ANT2; oflynn-frontside-26mm-cropped.jpg read by this lane

halo.text: AE2 — a 2-turn coil ETCHED on the outer annulus, ce-rf measures 0.2449 uH, tuned by C24/C25.

components.why: Same reason as the BLE antenna: copper on the board needs no carrier and no solder joint — and halo's annulus between the cell can and the contact lands is 0.70 mm wide, which holds two turns, not five, so the coil is eight times smaller than Nordic's reference and the tuning capacitors are eight times larger.

exact.buyable: Geometry not published. Same LDS process problem as row 15 — or, if the photograph is right and it is wound wire, a hand-wound coil and a bonding step.
exact.stack: Brings back the carrier and the central magnet well the coil is wound around.
exact.cost: CANNOT DETERMINE.
exact.schedule: As row 15.
exact.loses: Nothing measured. halo's coil inductance is modelled, Apple's is one of lane G's six open bench measurements and has never been measured by anyone in public.

apple.part: Integral patch, LDS on the carrier. Gain -1.6 dBi at 6.5 GHz, -0.6 dBi at 8 GHz.
apple.marking: Apple's FCC internal photo 6 labels the position "UWB Antenna"
apple.source: research/01 §3 ANT3 — Catley and Apple's FCC UWB test report E2V3

halo.text: ABSENT. No UWB radio, so no UWB antenna.

apple.part: A copper VOICE COIL glued to the plastic dome, moving against a FIXED CENTRAL MAGNET — the whole housing is the diaphragm. Driven by the MAX98357A across TP1 and TP38. NOT A PART ANYONE SELLS.
apple.package: custom motor assembly: coil + rare-earth magnet + the shell
apple.side: centre front, through the board's central hole
apple.source: research/01 §5 — iFixit ("the AirTag's body is essentially a speaker driver"), Catley; iFixit measured 78-80 dB at about 13 cm

halo.text: LS1 — a BARE Ø20.0 x 0.21 mm piezo bender BONDED TO THE INSIDE OF THE SHELL, driven anti-phase from two GPIO. Same trick, catalogue part.

components.why: Apple's answer is not buyable and a housed buzzer is 3.5 mm tall against the ~1.5 mm available, so halo keeps Apple's IDEA — the housing is the radiating surface — with a part a fifth of a millimetre thick.

exact.buyable: NO. There is no order code for Apple's motor. You would specify a coil (wire gauge, turns, former, bond), source a rare-earth magnet and a magnet well, and qualify a glue bond to a moulded dome — a custom assembly with its own tooling and its own line step.
exact.stack: It brings back the central magnet and the coil that D17 DELETED — the two parts whose removal freed the 1.742 mm halo spent on the 0.60 mm board and the 0.680 mm diaphragm gap. It also re-opens the annular board outline, because the magnet needs the hole.
exact.cost: CANNOT DETERMINE for the assembly. For scale, D11 priced the alternative — a real micro-speaker — at about $5.45, which is more than the rest of halo's board; halo's bender is $0.369 at a thousand.
exact.schedule: The longest single item in this table: a custom electro-acoustic part, its tooling, and an acoustic qualification.
exact.loses: It would ADD about 3.2 g — D17 measures halo at 7.8 g against the AirTag's 11 g and names Apple's motor as the whole difference. And iFixit found the piezo rivals were "just as much, if not more, noise": Apple chose the coil for sound QUALITY, not for volume, and halo is not selling sound quality.

components.inconsistency: electronics/halo_rev_a/schematic.py still carries LS1 = Murata 7BB-20-3, the part D20 declares end-of-life with zero authorized stock beyond 38 pieces at TTI. spec/bom-resolved.json resolves the line to the Same Sky CEB-2021 and marks it RESOLVED BY REPLACEMENT. The schematic has not caught up. Lane C1 does not own electronics/ and reports this rather than fixing it.

apple.part: CR2032 3 V lithium coin cell (Panasonic in the FCC test unit), on THREE sprung metal contacts: one negative on the floor of the well, two positive tabs on the wall. BOTH positives must see 3 V to boot; the left one powers the electronics, the right one is sensed at about 50 nA. NO CONNECTORS ANYWHERE ON THE PRODUCT.
apple.source: research/01 §2.2 and §6 — FCC internal photo 4; Catley; O'Flynn

halo.text: BT1 — CR2032 on THREE sprung C5191 fingers on halo's own three-pad land pattern (no bought holder exists under 2 mm). Pad 1 VDD at 12 o'clock, pads 2 and 3 at 4 and 8 o'clock. The third pad is VBAT_SNS_HI through a 4.7 M / 4.7 M divider — 319 nA at 3 V against Apple's ~50 nA. No connectors on the board either.

components.why: Apple's scheme reproduced: three contacts, two rails, one of them sensed rather than loaded, and not a connector on the product.

exact.buyable: The cell is a CR2032 either way. The CONTACTS are stamped metal on both products and neither is a catalogue part.
exact.stack: Already matched.
exact.cost: The sense divider is the only numeric difference: 4.7 M / 4.7 M draws 319 nA against Apple's ~50 nA. Two resistor values close it — 30 M / 30 M would reach 50 nA.
exact.schedule: One BOM edit, if it is worth 269 nA on a 2-microamp budget.

apple.part: Bare test pads. SWD fully exposed on TP30 (nRST) / TP35 (SWCLK) / TP36 (SWDIO) with SWO on TP31; the SPI flash fully exposed on TP19-TP24. APPROTECT is enabled but defeated by a voltage glitch on TP28. UNDOCUMENTED BY APPLE — the numbering is Colin O'Flynn's, not Apple's.
apple.marking: none — the names come from O'Flynn's map
apple.source: research/01 §7.1 — O'Flynn's test-point map, the de-facto standard

halo.text: J1 — a Tag-Connect TC2030 SWD footprint with a PUBLISHED PINOUT, plus 11 named test points (TP1-TP11), including SEPARATE FORCE AND SENSE pads on VDD and GND so a microamp sleep measurement is a genuine four-wire one, and two ASYMMETRIC fiducials so a Ø26 mm circle has a datum at all.

components.why: D6 point 3: certified tags from eufy and Motorola ship debug pads on the board but undocumented, and halo's differentiator is that ours is a header with a pinout.

exact.buyable: Bare pads cost nothing. Reproducing APPLE'S map exactly would mean matching a 38-pad numbering scheme invented by a third party for a board layout halo does not share.
exact.stack: Free.
exact.cost: $0. It is a documentation choice, not a part choice.
exact.schedule: n/a.
exact.loses: The four-wire force/sense pairs, which exist because a two-wire measurement puts the probe's own contact resistance in series with a single-digit-microamp reading.

apple.part: ABSENT. The AirTag broadcasts on Apple's network only.
apple.source: research/04 — no shipping product advertises both networks at once

halo.text: Both networks transmit in the SAME advertising event on all three channels. 2,888 bytes of flash and 116 of RAM. Written from Google's published specification byte for byte against its Tables 15 and 17.

components.why: Lane B found no open-source implementation of the Google network's tag side anywhere; halo appears to be the first.

apple.part: ABSENT. The AirTag ranges to a PHONE, never to another AirTag.
apple.source: research/01 §4; research/08

halo.text: Bluetooth Channel Sounding on the nRF54L10, specified at 6-20 cm line of sight and sub-metre in a real room on a 30 second update, with the accelerometer's orientation vector attached to every range. Tags report RAW RANGES with quality metadata, never solved positions.

apple.source: research/01 §2 — Catley's 26 mm disassembled envelope; O'Flynn's own 26 mm circle drawn on frontside-26mm-cropped.jpg
apple.conf: primary for the envelope, unverified for the exact figure

halo.note: the bounding extent of the Edge_Cuts geometry, measured by `fab dfm` and cross-checked on the exported Gerber (720 points)

pcb.why: 26.0000 mm on the major axis, inside Apple's stated ~26 mm. The minor axis is 25.6138 mm because three 26-degree keying notches cut to R12.60.

apple.source: research/01 §2 — O'Flynn, verbatim: "it's 0.3mm PCB so I'm pretty sure I broke some solder joints getting it out"

halo.note: read off the board's own stackup by `fab dfm`, not typed

pcb.why: TWICE Apple's, deliberately. D11a's piezo deletes Apple's magnet and voice coil, which returns 1.742 mm to the stack, and lane M spent part of it on a board that does not break when you handle it — the failure O'Flynn reports in the sentence above.

apple.value: NOT PUBLISHED. 4 is inferred from a 0.3 mm two-sided assembly with routed nets on both faces, and the dossier marks the inference UNVERIFIED. stacksmashing hosts merged layer pictures but states no count.

apple.value: ANNULAR — a round board with a large central hole carrying the magnet and the voice coil. Visible in every teardown photograph.

apple.value: 2. Front: battery contacts, voice-coil pads TP1/TP38, magnet well, NFC coil, the five 100 uF caps, the test-point field. Back: every IC, both crystals, the UWB module.

halo.value: 2. Bottom (B.Cu): the SoC, the accelerometer, both crystals, the four bulk capacitors, the DC-DC inductor, the NFC coil and the three battery contacts. Top (F.Cu): the passives, the 2.4 GHz antenna, the test points, the SWD footprint and the UWB stub.

apple.value: NONE, ANYWHERE. Every off-board connection is a spring contact or a soldered tab: 3 battery contacts, 6 antenna solder joints ("4x at upper center and 2x bottom left-of-center"), 2 voice-coil joints.
apple.source: research/01 §2.2 — O'Flynn's tear-off joint count

halo.value: NONE either. Three sprung battery fingers, two piezo wire lands, and zero antenna joints because the antennas are etched in the board.
halo.note: read off the schematic's connector-less contract

pcb.why: Same principle, and halo goes further: it has six fewer solder joints than Apple because the antennas are copper on the board rather than metal on a carrier.

apple.value: THREE antennas LASER-DIRECT-STRUCTURED onto the plastic carrier and SOLDERED to pads at the board edge. NFC has an extra return trace on the far side of the plastic with a via at each end. The board is soldered to the plastic tray and the antenna joints TEAR if you lift it: "Removing the PCB is likely to cause damage due to the thin PCB and being soldered to the plastic tray."
apple.source: research/01 §2 and §2.2 — Catley, O'Flynn

halo.value: TWO antennas ETCHED IN THE BOARD'S OWN COPPER. Zero solder joints, zero carrier, and the copper travels inside the KiCad design block so an integrator gets the routed antenna with the schematic.
halo.note: AE1 rim inverted-F on F.Cu; AE2 two-turn coil on B.Cu

pcb.why: TOGETHER WITH THE THICKNESS, THE DEEPEST DIVERGENCE IN THE PROJECT. Apple's scheme buys antenna volume outside the board at the cost of a tool, a plating line and six joints that break; halo's buys reproducibility and a distributable design block at the cost of antenna volume. D16 also names the limit: a design block carries no design rules, so halo's Ø37.31 mm keep-out has to travel as WORDS an integrator reads and applies — a block that places perfect copper into a host that floods ground over the antenna is worse than no block at all, because it looks correct.

apple.value: About 38 numbered pads, reachable after popping the back cover without removing the PCB — but the numbering is Colin O'Flynn's, not Apple's, and Apple documents none of it. SWD on TP30/35/36 + SWO on 31; the SPI flash on TP19-24; the glitch pad on TP28.

labels.scale_note: SCALE, stated rather than assumed. The two LEFT-HAND halo panels and the Apple FRONT panel are all cropped to the same 26 mm square and rendered at the same pixel size, 36.9 px/mm, so a millimetre is a millimetre across them — but the two scales are not the same KIND of number. halo's is MEASURED: 26.0000 mm on the major axis, read off the Edge_Cuts geometry of its own board file. Apple's is CITED: O'Flynn named his crop `frontside-26mm-cropped` and images/airtag/CATALOG.md records it as "cropped to the ~26 mm PCB diameter". The tilde is his and it is carried through — a circle least-squares fitted to the outermost feature in that frame comes out at 825 px across, which on the cited scale is 27.22 mm, consistent with a plastic carrier ring around a 26 mm board but not a confirmation of it. So: the two boards are the same diameter to the precision anyone has published, and no tighter comparison is available from any source in this repo. Apple's BACK photograph has NO scale reference of any kind — it is oblique, and a circular board images 2 460 x 2 760 px in it, an 11 percent difference between the axes. It is shown to fit, and no scale bar is drawn on it.
